newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST-Grolsch H1 net seen up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Grolsch H1 net seen up 10 pct.

text.p: Analysts expect Dutch brewer Grolsch NV to boost first-half net profits by some 10 percent as steady growth in U.K. sales and exports to Russia and France were seen compensating for adverse weather conditions.

Analysts polled by Reuters on Tuesday expected the company to post first half profits of between 19.8 million and 22.5 million guilders on Wednesday, with the forecast consensus at 21 million. The group posted first half net in 1995 of 18.9 million guilders.

"A negative point is the poorer weather conditions in 1996 so far compared with 1995," said ING analyst Gerard Rijk, who forecast a 19.8 million guilder first half net, at the bottom end of expectations.
"But on the positive side is the improvement in low margin exports to Russia and France...and increasing volumes in the U.K through their joint venture with Bass," he added.

Grolsch holds a 51 percent stake in Grolsch UK, a joint venture with Bass. Bass brews Grolsch premium beer under license and markets, distributes and sells the brand in the U.K., where sales, particularly in the take-home market, are rising.
But with Bass actually brewing the beer, analysts estimate up to 75 percent of profits from the U.K. to remain with the British brewer, leaving Grolsch with a limited share.

Analysts were upbeat on Grolsch's deal with Canada's Seagram Company Ltd for the exclusive distribution of Grolsch beer in the U.S. But they cautioned that the positive effects of the deal, agreed in February, would not be felt until 1997.

They were fairly positive about the company in the longer term, but emphasized that new distribution deals must be concluded if the company is to keep growing in the highly competitive international beer market.
"Grolsch are doing quite well with distribution agreements...but we now need a new move to ensure growth after 1997," ING's Rijk said.
